title: Treasury Repurchase Agreement Risk Management FAQs

source.name: New York Fed - Treasury Market Practices Group

summary: The Treasury Market Practices Group (TMPG) issued best practice recommendations for U.S. Treasury repo risk management, recommending that all repo transactions include haircuts or margin to mitigate counterparty credit, liquidity, and market risks. The guidance addresses risks in the non-centrally cleared bilateral repo market, where risk management practices lack consistency and transparency, potentially creating systemic risks. Implementation is recommended by June 2026.
key_points: TMPG recommends all Treasury repos include haircuts (or margin) alongside other risk management techniques such as position limits, netting agreements, and portfolio margining
Non-centrally cleared bilateral repo market lacks consistency and transparency in risk management practices
Working group included dealers, money funds, hedge funds, asset managers, financial market utilities, clearing banks, foreign central banks, Treasury Dept, and NY Fed staff
TMPG recommends implementation by June 2026 using a risk-based rolling approach prioritizing most material counterparty exposures
Centrally cleared repo already adheres to the best practice through CCP margining regimes
Not all repo transactions will be eligible for central clearing once mandatory clearing is in effect, leaving a segment of NCCBR market outside central clearing
why_it_matters: Weak risk management in the Treasury repo market can pose systemic risks if major participants default. This guidance aims to standardize haircuts and margin practices across bilateral repo transactions, reducing leverage opacity and improving financial system stability during market stress. Market participants handling material repo exposures should begin evaluating their legal agreements and policies now to meet the June 2026 deadline.
market_structure_context: This guidance directly addresses Treasury market plumbing by recommending standardized haircuts/margin for bilateral repo. It follows the 2022 TMPG white paper on clearing/settlement and a pilot data study by Treasury's Office of Financial Research on the non-centrally cleared bilateral repo market. The guidance complements SEC rule amendments expanding central clearing, which will cover some but not all repo volume.
